subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should OpenClaw ship floating per-agent macOS bubbles as a first-party native-app feature, or expose a supported macOS UI/window seam that allows this interaction to live outside core?
rationale: The request adds a new native desktop interaction model with persistent UI state and agent-routing implications; source-adjacent components do not establish a pre-approved product or extension boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a first-party macOS feature
options.body: Define the app-owned overlay, persistence, accessibility, and session-routing contract, then scope an implementation issue or PR.

options.title: Design an external UI seam
options.body: Specify a supported native macOS UI/window capability so an optional package can own the floating-bubble experience.

options.title: Defer the interaction model
options.body: Keep the request open without implementation until companion-app priorities and ownership capacity are confirmed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a first-party macOS feature
recommendation.body: Define the app-owned overlay, persistence, accessibility, and session-routing contract, then scope an implementation issue or PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history and prior review place this contributor closest to the adjacent macOS window, activity, and WebChat surfaces.
